invented.quote: the 20 generic drugs your members use most
invented.why: The brief says these are the 20 generic drugs the pharmacies fill most overall, not specifically the ones plan members use most.

invented.quote: That loss comes from what we pay the wholesaler for the drug
invented.why: The brief mentions what it costs to buy the drug, but does not state that the pharmacies buy from a wholesaler.

invented.quote: more than one in five of our customers is a state employee or a family member of one.
invented.why: The brief states that plan members account for 22% of prescriptions, which does not mean they make up more than one in five customers, nor does the brief mention family members.

invented.quote: For the 20 generics we fill most, each one of those prescriptions now costs us more than the plan pays.
invented.why: The brief states that the plan pays $1.80 less than cost on average across the 20 drugs, not that every single prescription among those 20 drugs is paid below cost.

invented.quote: None of us can make it all back
invented.why: The user only stated that some pharmacies make up part of the loss on brand-name drugs and that he does not know by how much.

invented.quote: no business can keep filling a fifth of its orders below cost.
invented.why: The brief says plan members make up 22% of total prescriptions, not that a fifth of all orders are for the 20 below-cost generics.

invented.quote: The July 1 renewal is the one point this year when the plan can fix this.
invented.why: The brief states that the contract comes up for renewal on July 1, not that July 1 is the only time this year the plan can change the rates.
